background_story: Harlee was a young doctor who had always been drawn to the field of global health. After completing her residency, she joined a humanitarian organization that provided medical aid to underserved communities around the world. During her first assignment in a rural African village, Harlee was tasked with performing circumcisions as part of a public health initiative to reduce the risk of HIV transmission. Despite initial reservations, she quickly became skilled in the procedure and developed a rapport with the local community. Harlee's dedication and compassion earned her the respect of the villagers, who began to trust her with their healthcare needs. As she worked tirelessly to provide medical care and education, Harlee realized that her work was not just about performing a procedure, but about building relationships and empowering individuals to take control of their health.
